name: Tesamorelin
route: Daily injection under the skin of the abdomen
status: FDA-approved (2010) to reduce excess abdominal fat in adults with HIV-associated lipodystrophy; not for weight loss
mechanism: Mimics growth hormone-releasing hormone so the pituitary gland releases more of its own growth hormone, which shrinks fat stored deep in the abdomen
uses: Excess belly fat in HIV-associated lipodystrophy

article.summary: Tesamorelin (Egrifta) is an FDA-approved daily injection that reduces deep belly fat in adults with HIV lipodystrophy. It is not for weight loss, and any use outside that group is off-label.
article.takeaway: Tesamorelin is a lab-made version of growth hormone-releasing hormone, the brain signal that tells the pituitary gland to release growth hormone. The FDA approved it in 2010 for one purpose: reducing excess abdominal fat in adults with HIV-associated lipodystrophy, a fat-distribution disorder linked to HIV and its treatment.[^1] In a 404-person trial, visceral fat (the deep fat around the organs) fell by **10.9% over 6 months** versus 0.6% on placebo, and the benefit faded when treatment stopped.[^2] It is not a weight-loss drug, and it is prohibited in competitive sport.
glance: Approved 2010 (Egrifta); current products are Egrifta SV and Egrifta WR
Excess abdominal fat in adults with HIV-associated lipodystrophy
Injection under the skin of the abdomen once a day
Placebo-controlled trials in HIV; a 2026 meta-analysis pooled five of them
Prohibited by WADA at all times

blocks.text: The hypothalamus, a control center at the base of the brain, releases growth hormone-releasing hormone (GHRH) in pulses. GHRH tells the pituitary gland to release growth hormone, which raises IGF-1, a growth factor made mainly by the liver.[^2] Tesamorelin is a 44-amino-acid analog of GHRH designed to act on the same receptor.

Growth hormone helps break down stored fat. In the main trial, deep abdominal (visceral) fat fell while limb fat and under-the-skin abdominal fat did not change.[^2] Tesamorelin does not supply growth hormone itself. It prompts the person's own pituitary gland to make more.
The approved use is narrow: reducing excess abdominal fat in adults with HIV who have lipodystrophy, a pattern in which fat builds up around the abdominal organs. The label lists three limits.[^1]

items: **Not for weight loss.** Its effect on weight is neutral, so it is not indicated for weight management
**Heart safety unproven.** Long-term cardiovascular safety has not been established
**No adherence claim.** There are no data showing it helps people stay on their HIV medicines

rows: 404 adults with HIV and excess abdominal fat
Visceral fat fell 10.9% vs 0.6% on placebo at 6 months, and about 18% in those who continued to 12 months[^2]
Visceral fat down 34 cm² vs up 8 cm² on placebo; liver fat also fell[^3]
5 placebo-controlled trials in adults with HIV
Visceral fat 27.7 cm² lower, lean mass 1.4 kg higher, no significant change in BMI[^4]

blocks.text: In the phase 3 extension, people switched from tesamorelin to placebo rapidly lost the visceral fat benefit.[^2] Blood sugar rose briefly early in the JAMA trial but did not differ from placebo by 6 months.[^3]

Tesamorelin comes as a powder that is mixed with the supplied liquid and injected under the skin of the abdomen once a day, rotating sites. Two products exist and are not interchangeable. Egrifta SV is dosed at 1.4 mg daily from a 2 mg vial that is mixed fresh each day.[^1] Egrifta WR is dosed at 1.28 mg daily from an 11.6 mg vial that is mixed once and used over 7 days.[^5]

items: **Most common** (over 5% in trials): joint pain, redness or itching at the injection site, pain in a limb, swelling from fluid retention and muscle aches[^1]
**Hormone effects:** it raises IGF-1, and the effects of long-term high levels are unknown, so levels are monitored[^1]
**Blood sugar:** glucose intolerance or diabetes can develop, so glucose is checked before and during treatment[^1]
**Other warnings:** fluid retention (including carpal tunnel syndrome), allergic reactions, an increased risk of neoplasms (growths) and higher risk of death in acute critical illness[^1]
**Not for people with** damage to the hypothalamic-pituitary axis, active cancer, a known allergy to the drug, or pregnancy[^1]

blocks.text: Tesamorelin was first approved in 2010 and is approved only for HIV-associated lipodystrophy.[^1] Use for general fat loss, muscle gain or anti-aging is off-label, and the randomized trials above enrolled adults with HIV, so the results do not automatically apply to others. Compounded and online versions are discussed under [compounded tesamorelin](/peptides/compounded-tesamorelin).

The World Anti-Doping Agency's 2026 Prohibited List bans growth hormone-releasing hormone analogs, including tesamorelin, at all times, so athletes subject to testing cannot use it without an approved exemption.

evidence.label: Strong for its approved use, narrower beyond it
evidence.text: Randomized, placebo-controlled trials in adults with HIV consistently show less visceral fat on tesamorelin,[^2][^3] and a 2026 meta-analysis of five trials agrees.[^4] The label notes that long-term cardiovascular safety is not established, and approval rests on trials in people with HIV.[^1]

faq.a: No. The label says it is not indicated for weight management because its effect on weight is neutral. It is aimed at visceral fat.[^1] The 2026 meta-analysis also found no significant change in BMI.[^4]

faq.q: What happens when someone stops tesamorelin?
faq.a: In the 12-month trial, people switched from tesamorelin to placebo quickly lost the visceral fat reduction they had gained.[^2]

faq.q: Is online or compounded tesamorelin the same as Egrifta?
faq.a: No. Egrifta SV and Egrifta WR are the FDA-approved products. Other versions are not FDA-approved and their quality is not reviewed by the agency; see [compounded tesamorelin](/peptides/compounded-tesamorelin).
Not without an exemption. WADA prohibits growth hormone-releasing hormone analogs, including tesamorelin, at all times.
